milestones.name: Where water lies is worked out on the CPU alone: a sea, a lake in a hollow and a channel with a current each have a level, a depth and a flow at every point
milestones.quality_bar: A description of water that a GPU, a game and a later river solver can all be held to: every answer follows from the bed and the declared bodies or from a closed form, as the reference queries of a shipped physics library do, and nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: From a bed height grid and declared bodies, `thrum-water-model` answers at any world point: the body of water there or none, its level, the bed, the depth and the current. A sea is level wherever the bed lies below it and beyond the bed's extent. A basin is the connected hollow round its seed below its level, and a second hollow beyond a ridge stays dry. A chart gives its own level and current where its level lies above the bed.
items.ask: Read the test. Are the expected answers closed forms worked out without the model: a cone-shaped hollow's shoreline radius at a level, a ridge between two hollows, a tilted chart? Would a model that floods every cell below the level, connected or not, fail it?

items.statement: Where declarations overlap, a chart is taken over a basin and a basin over the sea, and a basin's fill stops at a chart's footprint. Preparation refuses, by name: two bodies of one kind that overlap; a basin whose fill, anywhere in its stage's declared range, reaches the sea, another basin, the edge of the bed, or a chart other than across its end; and a chart with a cell on its footprint's edge whose neighbour is neither ground above the chart's level there nor a joined body's water at weight 1. Level, bed and current are continuous across the grid's cells.

Each body has a stage, inside a declared range, that is added to its level; a stage set outside the range is held at the range's end and counted. As a basin's stage rises its shoreline moves up the bed continuously, a neighbouring hollow floods only when the water reaches its sill, and lowering the stage drains it back to what it was.

Each body takes four gains, for the long waves and the three cascades, from its declared fetch and the wind through `thrum-sea-model`'s spectrum. The most exposed body's are 1; none exceeds 1; each falls as the fetch shortens; at 10 m/s the long-wave gain is under 0.05 for a fetch of 5 km and the shortest cascade's is over 0.9 at 200 m. A swell adds nothing to a basin's or a chart's own gains: with a swell running and no wind their long-wave gain is zero, and adding a swell to a wind never raises the energy their long waves carry.
items.ask: Are the expected gains worked out in the test from fetch-limited growth relations and band integrals of its own, and not from the function under test?

items.statement: At any point each wave layer is held, longest first, so that its significant height is at most 0.6 of the depth plus the swash depth there: untouched in deep water, a remainder at the still waterline, nothing where the ground stands a swash depth above the level, and continuous between. The swash depth is the profile's ratio times the significant height the point's row gives the field at its gains, before the limit, never more than the margin height and zero with no waves. It is one value over a body away from a join and follows the mix inside one. The power the limit takes from each layer is reported, and is zero where the limit does not bind.

The f64 surface model gives, for a point and a time, the water's height (the level and each wave layer at its gain), its slope, the surface's velocity (the current and the waves' together) and the time derivative of height, and says the point is dry whenever the surface there does not stand above the bed: on ground beyond the water, and in the swash between waves. On an open sea it equals `thrum-sea-model`'s evaluator, and on a basin whose gains are zero it is the level.

A conformance harness takes any provider of water answers and reports its largest difference from the model in height, slope, velocity, depth and current over a stated set of points and ticks, and every point where the two disagree on the body or on wet and dry. Given the model it reports nothing; given the model with one basin's level moved by a centimetre, it reports that centimetre and the points the shoreline crossed.

A bed grid built from triangles holds in each cell the highest ground over the cell's centre. Built from a tilted plane and from a bowl, it matches their closed forms to within the height the ground spans across one cell.
`thrum-water-model` builds and its tests run with no graphics device and no dependency on `thrum-render` or `wgpu`, and it holds no preset, island, hull or water table.

A chart meets the bodies it joins with no step. At every point on a source end's or a mouth's edge the chart's mixed row equals the joined body's row, in level, current and every gain, and so does what follows from the row: the swash depth, the wave support and the surface's height after the depth limit. That holds under a swell and a wind, with the source's stage and the mouth's each at both ends of its range, at an end too deep for the limit to bind and at one 0.25 m deep. Wherever the receiving body's level plus the design's reach, 0.175 of the margin height, stands at or above the chart's own level, the chart's row is that body's, and the weight toward it falls smoothly to nothing over the 0.25 m above. Inside the footprint, away from the ends, the row is the chart's own.
items.ask: Read the test. Does it compare the surface after the depth limit either side of each end, for a lake raised and lowered and a tide raised and lowered, under a swell, at a shallow end as well as a deep one? Would taking the chart over its neighbours with one stage of its own fail it, and would a swash depth kept once for each body fail it at the shallow mouth, as part K of `docs/evidence/WATERS/design-proof/water_proof.py` shows for both?

items.statement: The map names a body on its still water and on its shore margin: ground that rises from its waterline to the margin height, reached without descending, so a hollow beyond a ridge is never in it. On a plane beach under one regular wave the model's waterline, where its surface meets the bed, runs up and back each period between the heights the design's closed form gives, 0.175 of the swash depth above the level and 0.27 of it below, and does not move when the swash ratio is zero.
items.ask: Are the expected heights the closed form, worked out in the test without the model, and would a limit that takes the waves to nothing at the still waterline fail it?

milestones.name: On the CPU alone, a swell turns to face a beach, closes up, rises and breaks where the depth says, and an island calms its lee
milestones.quality_bar: Wave theory a coastal engineer would sign: every figure follows from the bed, the dispersion relation and a published breaking rule, held to closed forms on a plane beach as the nearshore models SWAN and XBeach are, and nothing in it needs a graphics device.

items.statement: For a still body over a bed, preparation gives each of the wave lattice's eight directions a lag at wavelengths a factor of two apart from 20 m to 640 m and at stages 0.5 m apart across the body's declared range. The lag is zero on the bed's edge and beyond it. On a plane beach of 1 in 10 on 2 m cells, an 80 m wave's phase at 0°, 30° and 60° of incidence is within 0.5 rad of Snell's closed form, where the design measured 0.34, and its crests in 2 m of water lie within 1° of Snell's angle.
items.ask: Read the test. Is the expected phase the integral of Snell's law, worked out in the test without the model's solver? Would a wave that keeps its deep-water phase fail it, and one given the local depth's wavenumber at each point with no integral along its path?

items.statement: A component whose wavelength lies between two of those, and a stage between two samples, take the blend. On plane beaches of 1 in 10 and 1 in 30, for wavelengths from 20 m to 640 m and every stage in a 2 m range, the gradient of the blended phase is within 3% of the dispersion relation's wavenumber in a metre of water or more, where the design measured 2.0% and 2.6%, and within 10% between the 0.5 m floor and a metre, where it measured 7.9%. Moving the stage through a sample leaves no step in the phase.

Ground above the shore margin is closed to the lag, so round an island a wave reaches every shore from the sea: wherever a component's exposure is above zero and the water is under 4 m deep, its direction of travel lies within 75° of the shore's inward normal, where the design measured 60° at most and the untransformed wave runs out of the land on the lee side. A component's exposure is the share of its 45° sector with open water behind it, 1 on the windward shore and 0 in the lee, its energy is scaled by it, and far downwind of the island it returns toward 1.
items.ask: Does the test's island have a lee the deep-water wave leaves through, and are the expected exposures worked out in the test from the island's outline?

items.statement: A transformed component's height follows linear theory's shoaling coefficient at the point's depth, and the long layer is then held by the depth limit as M1.5 holds it. A crest's breaking index is twice the envelope of the transformed long waves, before the limit, over 0.78 of the still depth. On a plane beach a regular wave of 1 m and 8 s reaches a breaking index of 1 in the depth linear shoaling gives, 1.64 m, at a height within 10% of Komar and Gaughan's 1.41 m, where the design measured 9% under. In a sea of two trains the highest crests of a set reach an index of 1 in deeper water than the lowest.
items.ask: Is the expected break depth worked out in the test from the dispersion relation and the group velocity, without the model?

items.statement: The breaker section is the profile's table over phase and breaking index, and the model refuses a table that breaks the design's rules: it adds nothing at index 0; its throw at each index is a function of the section's height that never falls as the height rises; past the bore index it has no throw and its crest and trough stand at the plain wave's heights. With the first profile's table the surface through a breaking crest overhangs near an index of 1 and never crosses itself. Inshore of the depth the waterline draws back to, the surface is the plain limited wave: M1.13's beach gives the same waterline heights with surf in the profile.
items.ask: Does the test run M1.13's plane beach with surf in the profile and hold the waterline's highest and lowest reach to the closed form? Does it search the thrown curve for a crossing at every index, and not only at 1?

items.statement: With surf in the profile the f64 surface model gives the height, slope, surface velocity and rate of height of the transformed and shaped surface, the highest surface where a crest overhangs, and says where a point is dry. Without surf every answer is M1's to the last bit. On a sea with no bed in reach the answers with and without surf are the same. The conformance harness reports a provider that leaves the transform out by the points where it differs.

Inside a chart's join the shore transform is the joined body's, taken at the join's weight, so M1.12 holds with surf in the profile: under a swell and a wind, at each end's edge, the surface after the transform, the section and the depth limit is the same either side, at a deep end and at one 0.25 m deep, with each stage at both ends of its range.

What the transform costs to prepare is on record in `docs/evidence/WATERS/M12-preparation.md`: for a 1 km bed on 4 m cells with a 2 m range of stage, on this Mac, the time to solve the lags and exposures and the bytes they occupy. No figure in the record decides this item.
items.ask: Does the record give the time and the bytes with the commit and the load on the machine, and say how each grows with the bed's cells and the stage's range?

milestones.name: A float and a small craft ride the waves they sit on, at sea and on the lake, from rest to 15 m/s, and a float in a current is carried by it
milestones.quality_bar: Boats and barrels as in the sea of Sea of Thieves: they lift as a crest arrives, tilt down its face, and never slide, jitter or lag the water. On the lake they sit as still as the water, and in a current they go with it.

items.statement: One dispatch per tick answers every posted point with height, slope, surface velocity and the time derivative of height, valid at the point's use tick, with that tick, the times its layers were made from and a support flag for each layer. For 2,048 points on a gale the long-wave part matches the model at the use tick within 2 mm, and the cascade part matches the model's cascades at the frame's time, carried to the use tick by their rate of change, within `SEA` M2's bound, with each point's footprint choosing the cascade mip. Each answer also names the body of water at its point with the depth and the current there, as the CPU model gives them, and a point where the surface at the use tick does not stand above the bed says it is dry, on ground beyond the water and in the swash between waves.

At a 60 Hz tick and 120 Hz frames an answer reaches the game one to two ticks after it was asked for, through discarded frames and a stalled readback. An answer used at another tick than its use tick is moved once, by its time derivative, and counted. An answer older than the declared maximum is unavailable and counted, and the blocking-read counter stays at zero.
items.ask: Is there any map, poll or readback in `thrum-water` or the example that waits for the GPU? Is the counter raised at every place that could?

items.statement: A request over the profile's capacity is refused whole, by body in ID order, counted and shown in the scene's status. A body whose generation changed never receives an answer posted for the old one.

On a glassy sea the craft and the eight floats settle to their hydrostatic drafts and stay there. Through ten minutes of gale, with the craft held at rest, at 5 m/s and at 15 m/s, no body leaves the surface, sinks, capsizes, or gains energy that the waves and its thrust did not give it.
items.ask: Read the test. Is the energy bound worked out from the wave field and the thrust, and would a body driven by a fixed bobbing schedule fail it?

items.statement: A float and the craft rise, pitch and roll with the waves under them: a float lifts as a crest reaches it and tilts down its face, the craft pitches into a head sea and rolls in a beam sea, and nothing slides, jitters or lags the water. This holds at rest, at 5 m/s and at 15 m/s, in a trade wind and in a gale.

milestones.name: The craft leaves a wake that spreads behind it, outlives it and lifts a float it crosses, and a stone dropped in the lake sends rings that slow in the shallows and die at the shore
milestones.quality_bar: A wake made of water, past the foam trail of the sea of Sea of Thieves: arms and crests that spread at the right angle for the speed, stay where they were made through a turn, travel on after the craft stops, and rock a float in their path. On a lake, rings as on any still pond: round, slowing and bunching toward the shallows, gone at the shore.

items.statement: The f64 wake reference in `thrum-water-model`, forced on deep water by the moving Gaussian pressure patch of `docs/evidence/SEA/design-proof/wake_proof.py` (6 m long, 2 m wide), gives a transverse wavelength within 5% of 2πU²/g at 3 m/s and at 6 m/s, a ridge within 3° of 19.47° at 3 m/s and narrower than 19.47° at 6 m/s. After the source is removed a crest travels on at its phase speed.

The interaction reference steps height and potential by the design's finite-depth update and depth ladder. A wave on uniform depth at a ladder depth neither grows nor shrinks. Over each level's band, on uniform depths from the level's first depth to deep and midway between ladder depths, in steps of one tick and of eight, a wave's phase speed is within 3% of √(g·tanh(kd)/k) and its group speed within 6%, where the design measured 2.1% and 4.4%. Across a window that holds 0.125 m shallows and 10 m of water, packets of 30 m, 60 m and 100 m cross the 10 m part within 6% of the true group speed, where the design measured 3.9%. On beds of varying depth with dry patches, undamped, the sum of squared height stays under 1.25 times its start for 120 s, where the design measured 1.08 on a shoaling beach. On deep water the step is eWave's.
items.ask: Does the test step fields through beds that vary and measure speed from a crest's or a packet's travel? Would it fail for one operator at the window's mean depth, and for eWave's equations 19 and 20 with only the frequency replaced?

items.statement: On Metal the two-level wake follows the reference through a straight run, a turn, a coast and a restart: inside the near window, clear of its border, it differs by under 5% of the field's RMS height. No wave is carried by both levels, and none re-enters a window from its far side.
items.ask: Is the reference a single fine level with the same source, and does the test fail when both levels are given the whole source?

items.statement: No wave crosses ground between two waters. On Metal, with a 2 m bar of ground across a window and 4 m of water at its foot, a ring raised on one side leaves the height and potential of the water on the other side exactly at rest, where one transform over the whole window carries 3% of the ring's peak across. A ring that reaches a shore dies there, with under a tenth of its energy coming back, where the design measured 2.4%, and a window half on land keeps its waves on the wet half. A region beyond the profile's count of solves is at rest, and its sources are refused in order, counted and shown in the scene's status. In a uniform current a ring's centre moves with the current as the ring spreads.
items.ask: Does the test read the state of the water beyond the bar, not of the land, and does it fail when the window is solved as one region?

items.statement: An impulse record the game posts raises a ring at its place on the tick it names, larger for a larger impulse, once. Records over the profile's capacity are refused in ID order, counted and shown in the scene's status.

A body's wake comes from the vertical force the water put on it, spread over its footprint. The craft at rest on a glassy sea settles to the same draft with the wake on as with it off, and raises no waves once settled. Body records over the profile's source capacity are refused in ID order, counted and shown in the scene's status.

A float 20 m to one side of the craft's track on a glassy sea rises and falls as the wake's crests reach it, at the times the reference gives for its position, and is still again when the wake has passed.

At 3 m/s two arms spread behind the craft with transverse crests between them; at 12 m/s the wake is narrower; through a turn the old wake stays where it was made and keeps spreading; after the craft stops the waves travel on and fade; a float on the track rocks as they cross.

items.statement: In a trade wind the wake rides the waves: no window edge shows, no seam shows where the fine wake ends, and nothing pops as the windows move with the craft.
items.inspect: A `realtime` sequence following the craft at 6 m/s in a trade wind from 40 m above: the windows' edges, and the water about 30 m behind the craft, where the fine wake ends.

items.statement: A stone dropped into the lake sends round rings that spread, slow and bunch as they reach the shallows and die at the shore. The craft's wake on the lake stays in the lake: nothing shows on the pond beside it or on the sea beyond the ground between them.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences from the lake's shore at 2 m and from 40 m above: a stone's rings from the drop to the shore, and the craft crossing the lake at 3 m/s.

items.statement: In Chrome the craft's wake spreads, outlives it and lifts the float, a stone's rings die at the lake's shore, and the interaction waves match the reference within M6.3's bound.

items.statement: After every submitted frame the wake's two endpoints hold what the design's endpoint table gives: the committed tick's wake and the wake of the tick committed before it, each with its tick. A hitch of up to eight ticks is one wake step. With a hitch of eight ticks every second, the wake after 20 s differs from the same run stepped tick by tick by under 2% of the field's RMS height, where the design measured 0.6%. Ticks beyond eight are counted as dropped. A backward tick, a new timeline and a replaced device reset the wake to calm and the scene's status says so. A discarded frame and a capture frame change nothing.

milestones.name: Whitecaps form as the wind rises, the craft leaves a foam trail that drifts, spreads and fades, and foam forms where the sea dies on the beach
milestones.quality_bar: Foam as in the sea of Sea of Thieves: bright caps with soft edges on breaking crests, streaks left behind them, a white churn at the hull with pale turquoise water under it, a trail that widens to lace and is gone in about a minute, and no stamped or repeated shape anywhere. On the beach, a ragged band of foam where the waves die, washed up the sand as lace.

items.statement: The foam reference in `thrum-water-model` holds the four stocks and moves material only along the design's transfers. With no birth, aged film gains what fresh film loses, surfacing air becomes fresh film once, aged film rises out of fresh film and fresh film out of submerged air before they fall, the inventory of film and yield-weighted air never rises, and every stock ends at nothing. A birth never takes cover past one.
items.ask: Are the expected values the closed form of the transfer chain, worked out without the reference? Would a model that only decays each stock fail the test?

items.statement: On Metal the foam follows the reference for a scripted set of causes. A patch moves by the distance the drift gives: under a wind, and up a plane beach the test makes under one regular wave, where the rising sheet carries it as the reference does. A window shift neither loses nor doubles foam inside the window.
Foam is carried by the map's current: in a chart with a uniform current a patch moves by the distance the current gives. Foam on ground the water has left stays where it is and ages out.

On a glassy sea with the craft at rest every stock stays at zero for ten minutes, on the sea and on the lake. Mean foam cover on the sea rises with wind across a fresh breeze, a strong breeze and a gale.

Foam is born where the depth takes power from the waves, in proportion to that power, and only where the surface stands above the bed. In a trade wind a band of foam forms along the example's beach, from where the swell is first held to the top of the swash, and more in a gale. On the lake's shore in the same wind the foam born is the share of the beach's that the power its own waves lose gives, which is a small one. None forms in a calm, or anywhere with the waves left out.
items.ask: Is the shore's birth rate taken from the power the depth limit reports, and not from the distance to the shore or the depth alone? Is the lake's foam compared with the share its lost power gives, and not with zero?

items.statement: After the craft has passed at 6 m/s and been removed, its trail stays where the water carried it for at least the aged film's lifetime, and is wider and thinner at each later reading.

In a gale, whitecaps form on breaking crests with a bright core and a feathered edge, stay behind the crest as streaks, and fade. A fresh breeze shows fewer and a glassy sea none. No stamp, grid or repeated shape shows from 2 m or from 40 m, and whitecaps thin toward the horizon with no line where the foam's windows end.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills and a `realtime` sequence at each wind, from 2 m and 40 m: single caps, the water behind a breaking crest, two places a pattern length apart, and the far sea.

items.statement: The craft's trail is white where the hull meets the water and behind the stern, with pale turquoise water under and beside the foam; it turns to lace as it ages, widens, thins, and is gone in about a minute. At rest there is none.
items.inspect: A `realtime` sequence from a chase view and from 40 m above, of the craft at 6 m/s and 12 m/s on a calm sea and then stopping: the hull's waterline, the stern, and the trail over the minute after the craft passes.

items.statement: On the beach in a trade wind and a gale, foam forms through the band where the waves die, rides the sheet of water up the sand, and is left as lace on the wet sand when the sheet draws back, where it thins and fades. The sand the waves wash holds a wet sheen that fades toward their highest reach, with no edge, flicker or floating film at any angle. No stamped line follows the shore, and the lake's shore shows at most a thin broken edge.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills and a `realtime` sequence of the beach from 2 m on the sand and from 40 m above, in each wind: the band where waves die, the waterline, and the lake's shore for comparison.

items.statement: The foam pattern is a cooked product of the example, lent through a lease. An edit to it shows in the running scene with the water's foam history marked invalid once. Before the lease is resident and after a device loss the water draws without it.
In Chrome whitecaps form with the wind, the trail outlives the craft, and the foam follows the reference.

With foam running in a gale, at sea and at the beach, the paired cost record is taken again at 2560×1440, beside the last record for the same views. Each tripwire it trips has its investigation beside it. No figure in the record decides this item.

items.statement: After every submitted frame the foam's two endpoints hold what the design's endpoint table gives. A hitch of up to eight ticks is one foam step: after it the transfers and births match the reference stepped tick by tick as M7.2 holds them, and a drifting patch is where the drift carries it. Ticks beyond eight are counted as dropped. A backward tick, a new timeline and a replaced device reset the foam to none. A discarded frame and a capture frame change nothing.
Every registered exact baseline, on the Mac and in Chrome, passes the verifier at the claimed commit: this milestone moved no retained image.

The film on sand the waves wash is drawn and is not water. It appears only inside wave support, where the surface stands below the ground, with a weight of 1 at the still waterline that reaches 0 at the height the design gives. A query point under it answers dry, no foam is born on it, and foam the sheet left there ages out as the reference gives. With the waves left out there is no film. It writes no scene depth: under it the depth is the ground's.
items.ask: Does the test read the query's answer, the foam's births and the written depth under the film, and not only the film's drawn weight?

items.statement: The foam reference carries foam up a beach with the swash. On a plane beach of 1 in 10 under one regular wave, with no wind and no current, a thin patch laid between the draw-back line and the still waterline moves up the sand while the sheet over it rises and stays where it is while the sheet falls; after three waves its centre lies within 0.5 m of the model's run-up line, and it has lost no foam but what the chain aged away. A patch seaward of the draw-back line does not move, and no patch moves with the swash ratio at zero or the waves left out.
items.ask: Is the expected path worked out in the test by following parcels under the design's rule from the surface model's height and the bed, and not read from the reference's own drift? Would a transport with only the current's and the wind's drift fail it, as the first grid row of part M of `docs/evidence/WATERS/design-proof/water_proof.py` does?

milestones.name: Swell turns to face the beach, rises and breaks into white water that runs up the sand, on the Mac and in Chrome
milestones.quality_bar: Surf as on the beaches of Horizon Forbidden West: lines of swell that bend to the shore and stack up, crests that steepen, pitch and go white along their length, a bore of foam that runs in and dies in the swash, the bigger waves of a set breaking further out. No wave walking out of the land, no curtain at the waterline, no torn or stair-stepped crest, no foam stamped along the shore.

items.statement: On Metal the long waves over a bed are the model's. For a bed the test makes, with surf in the profile, the field cache's displaced surface and the query's answers at 4,096 points from deep water to the swash, on tick frames and repeat frames and at stages between two samples, match `thrum-water-model`. The largest differences are recorded, and the test holds those recorded bounds.
items.ask: Were the bounds written from a measurement on this Mac, in the record with its date and commit, and are they small beside a wave's height where it breaks? Does the test fail when the lag is left out, and when the section is?

items.statement: Surf is a capability. A profile without it creates no lag or exposure texture, makes none of their reads and evaluates no section.

A float rides the crest the surface shows. In the surf on a plane beach the test makes, a float's answers are the model's at its use tick, the highest surface where a crest overhangs, and a float carried into the swash reads dry between waves and wet under each.
items.ask: Is the float's expected height taken from `thrum-water-model` with surf in the profile, and would a query that left the transform out fail?

items.statement: The island has a beach open to the swell. In a trade wind with a 10 s swell arriving about 45° off the beach, the swell's lines turn to face the beach as they come in, close up and stand taller. No wave runs along the shore or out of the land, and no step shows in the swell where the bed begins.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills and a `realtime` sequence from 40 m above the beach and from 2 m on the sand: the swell's lines from deep water to the break, and the water over the bed's edge.

items.statement: A crest steepens on its front, pitches forward and breaks, the largest of a set furthest out and the break running along the crest. Behind the break a bore runs in, lower as the water shallows, and ends in the swash. Nothing stands as a wall at the waterline, and no crest is torn, stair-stepped or folded through itself, from the sand, from 40 m above or from 1 km off.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences in a trade wind and a gale with the swell running, from 2 m on the sand looking along the break and out to sea, from 40 m above, and from 1 km off shore: single crests through their break, frame by frame.

items.statement: With surf, the foam that the long waves' lost power gives is born where a crest spends it: on the front face of a crest whose breaking index is past 1, and as submerged air under its lip. Summed over a wave the birth is what M7.5's rule gives for the same power, and in a calm or with the waves left out there is none. Beyond the foam's far level a beach's cover is the steady state of the same power.
items.ask: Is the birth compared with the power the depth limit reports, wave by wave, and does the test fail for a birth spread evenly over the wave?

items.statement: The breaking crest whitens at its lip and down its face and leaves pale water and lace behind it. The bore's white front travels with it into the swash, where the foam is carried up the sand. A far beach keeps its line of surf, with no edge where the foam's windows end. A calm sea shows none.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills and `realtime` sequences of the beach in a calm, a trade wind and a gale, from 2 m on the sand, from 40 m above and from 1 km off: the lip, the water behind a broken crest, the bore's front and the swash.

items.statement: The island shelters its lee. In a trade wind the lee beach laps with short waves and no swell while the windward beach breaks, the swell's lines bend round the headland, and far downwind the sea is whole again with no edge to the calm. As the tide is moved through its range the surf keeps its place against the waterline, with no jump.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills from 40 m over the windward beach, the lee beach and the headland and from 300 m above the whole island, in a trade wind; and a `realtime` sequence of the windward beach while the tide control is moved through its range.

items.statement: The breaking crest keeps the frame contract: in submitted frames its pixels carry the depth of the displaced sheet, the nearest surface where a crest overhangs, and motion equal to the model's displacement between presentations through the break. Moving the stage marks the water's history invalid no more often than the design's reset rule gives.
In Chrome the surf draws with no validation error, inside the sampled textures and storage of the recorded capability record, and the transformed field matches the model within M13.1's bounds.

milestones.name: Water reflects the sky, the Sun, its shores and the craft, shows the ground and hulls beneath it, glitters and dims under a cloud's shade, from dawn to night
milestones.quality_bar: Water optics as in the sea of Sea of Thieves and the skies of Red Dead Redemption 2 over it: a glitter path under the Sun, sky colour in the swell, a hull seen green through the water at its waterline, shade that takes the sparkle and leaves the sky's light. On the lake, the still water of Red Dead Redemption 2: the far shore and hills mirrored at dawn, stones on the bed seen through the shallows, deepening to the water's own colour.

items.statement: At dawn, noon, low Sun, twilight and night the sea reflects that hour's sky, the Sun's glitter lies under the Sun and widens as the wind rises, the night sea is dark under the sky's glow, and nothing clips to flat white or black.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at the five hours in a calm, a trade wind and a gale, from 2 m and 40 m: the glitter path, the swell's faces and the horizon.

items.statement: The craft's hull below its waterline and a sunk float are seen through the water, tinted and fading with depth. The waterline on the hull is a soft edge. Thin crests between the camera and a low Sun glow.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at noon in a calm, from 2 m and 6 m, of the craft at rest and of floats sunk 0.5 m and 2 m; and of crests against a low Sun in a trade wind.

items.statement: At the lake's edge, the pond and off the beach the ground shows through the shallows, tinted and fading with depth until the water's own colour hides it. The waterline is a soft edge with no bright or dark rim, and the bed moves under passing waves no more than refraction gives.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at noon and low Sun from 2 m on each shore, looking down into the shallows and along the waterline, and a `realtime` sequence of small waves over the lake's shallows.

items.statement: On calm water the craft and the floats reflect in the sea beside them, each reflection whole from the waterline to the image of the body's top. Where a reflection leaves the screen, passes its reach or meets the sky it falls back to the sky with no hole, streak or edge.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills and a `realtime` pan of the craft and floats on a glassy sea at low Sun, from 2 m and 10 m above: each reflection, and the screen's edges during the pan.

items.statement: On the calm lake the far shore, the hills and a tree on the bank reflect in the water wherever they are on screen, each joined to its foot at the waterline. Until the mirror view of M14, where a reflection's source is off the screen or hidden, or the water is too rough to mirror, the water shows the sky with no hole, streak or stretched edge, and a breeze blurs the reflection away smoothly.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills of the lake at dawn and noon in a calm from 2 m and 10 m, a `realtime` pan and tilt that takes the far shore off the screen, and a `realtime` sequence as the wind rises from calm to a breeze.

items.statement: With a cloud optical-depth provider present, direct sunlight on the sea is dimmed once by the provider's factor: the glitter, the sunlit water colour and the foam's sunlit part. Sky-lit terms are not dimmed. With no provider the sea's shader and its pixels are unchanged.
items.inspect: `fixed` stills at noon with a labelled stand-in provider's shade crossing the sea and the grey float: the shade's edge on the water and on the float.

items.statement: The gather copies opaque colour and depth only inside the rectangles its readers need: registered bodies on screen, water thin enough to see through, and the screen while water still enough to mirror is in view. On an open sea with no body on screen it does not run. Every water pixel that reads the gather reads inside what was copied, and every water pixel whose reflected or refracted ray meets a registered body within the design's reach and slope allowance lies inside that body's receiving rectangle. A scene with no water compiles to the same passes and storage as before.
items.ask: Does the test hold the receiving rectangles to rays reflected and refracted on the CPU, from cameras 1 m to 40 m up, on flat water and with waves, including a body whose reflection lies wholly outside its own source rectangle? Does it hold the see-through rectangles to the map's depths and the water type's sight depth?

items.statement: A matte panel of known radiance, reflected in flat water and seen through it, and a matte bed of known radiance under 0.5 m and 3 m of water, give the stored colour the design's optics equation gives, to within the half-float step and the design's declared approximations. This holds at exposure scales sixteen times apart, where the colour divided by the scale does not change, and with the panel 20 m and 3 km from the camera.
items.ask: Is the expected colour worked out on the CPU from the panel's and the bed's radiance, the lent aerial values and the water table, without the water's shader? Would reading the copied scene colour as radiance, or dividing out the exposure alone, fail it at 3 km?

items.inspect: `fixed` stills in Chrome at noon, low Sun and night at those items' views, judged by their lists and against the Mac's portable recipe.

milestones.name: Water runs down a channel from the lake to the sea: its surface follows the slope, its ripples and foam travel with the current, and a float is carried down to the sea
milestones.quality_bar: A running stream as in Red Dead Redemption 2: water that visibly moves downstream at its own speed, faster in the narrows, carrying foam and anything afloat, with no sliding sheet, pulse or seam where it joins still water.

items.statement: The example has a channel from the lake to the sea whose chart is made by hand and labelled a stand-in for `RIVERS`' solver, with a source end on the lake and a mouth on the sea. The drawn surface stands at the map's level along its whole fall. In a trade wind with a swell running, and again with the lake's level and the tide each at both ends of its range, the depth the water writes either side of each end's edge differs by no more than `thrum-water-model`'s surface does between those places, beyond the bound M4.1 recorded: no step, gap or doubled water at either join. That holds at low tide too, when the water at the mouth is shallow enough for the depth limit to hold the swell. At high tide the lower channel is the sea's water.
items.ask: Is the channel reached only through the chart a game can declare, with no code path in `thrum-water` that knows it is the example's or a stand-in? Does the test fail when the chart is taken over its neighbours with one stage of its own? At low tide, does the depth limit hold the swell at the mouth in the test's own readings?

items.statement: Surface detail in a current is carried by it. Tracked across submitted frames where the chart's current is 0.5 m/s and 1.5 m/s, the detail's speed downstream is recorded against the current, and the test holds that recorded bound; in still water it does not move.
items.ask: Is the recorded difference under a tenth of the current, and is it larger than the tracking's own error, measured on still water? Was the bound written from a measurement on this Mac, in the record with its date and commit?

items.statement: The channel reads as running water: ripples and foam move downstream, faster where the channel narrows, with no texture sliding as one sheet and no pulse at the carriage's period. Where it leaves the lake and where it meets the sea there is no seam, step or change of look, in a swell and while the lake's level and the tide are moved.
items.inspect: `realtime` sequences from the bank at 2 m, looking across and along the channel, at its narrows and at each end, one of each end while the lake's level and the tide are moved through their ranges in a trade wind with a swell running, the mouth held at low tide among them, and one from 40 m above its whole length.

items.statement: A float released at the top is carried down the channel and out into the sea, and its answers pass from the chart to the sea with no step in level or current. A post standing in the current trails foam downstream of it, with none upstream and none when the current is set to nothing.
In Chrome the channel draws, its detail is carried and the float reaches the sea.
A chart is documented as the seam a river solver writes: its grid and cell size, and the level, current and loss of height with their units, signs and what each reader does with them.
items.ask: Could `RIVERS`' planner have a solver write a chart from this documentation and the design alone? Does it say what a chart's stage changes and what it leaves as prepared?

items.statement: A pixel is under water exactly when its own point on the near plane lies below the displaced surface there. While the whole lens is above the water none of the capability's passes runs.

items.statement: Light under water is the design's equation. A matte panel of known radiance seen through 1 m and 8 m of water, level and looking down, a matte bed seen from under water, and a panel standing above the water seen through the surface from beneath inside the window, give the stored colour the equation gives, to within the half-float step and the declared approximations, at exposure scales sixteen times apart. Outside the window nothing above the water shows.
items.ask: Is the expected colour worked out on the CPU from the panel's radiance, the water table and the lent aerial values, without the water's shader? Would composing the water over a pixel twice fail it?

items.statement: Looking up through calm water, the sky, the bank and the craft's hull at its waterline show inside a bright disc about the vertical, squeezed toward its rim, and outside it the surface mirrors the water below. Waves break the rim into moving shards with no hole, streak or hard seam, and foam overhead is a pale ceiling.

items.statement: Under water the bed, the hull and a sunk float are seen through water that takes their colour toward its own with distance. Deeper water is darker, the lake differs from the sea as their water types do, and nothing clips to flat black or white at dawn, noon or twilight.

milestones.name: A visitor takes the water from glassy calm to gale, raises and lowers the lake, and goes from dawn to night with the controls, and it holds up in motion, on the Mac and in Chrome
milestones.quality_bar: The whole range of the sea of Sea of Thieves: a mirror calm, a working breeze and a gale under any hour's sky, from the deck and from the masthead, with a vista to the horizon, stable under temporal reconstruction as a shipped game's water is. The lake and the channel hold across the same range.

items.statement: Wind speed and direction, swell height, period and direction, the tide and the lake's level, time of day and a field overlay are typed controls with the same keys, labels, units and ranges on the Mac panel and the Chrome page. A parameter file applies them, and five presets from glassy calm to gale apply on both with nothing refused.
In Chrome the page declares the same controls, and each preset and a parameter file apply.

milestones.name: Still water mirrors the hills, trees and far shore that the camera cannot see, on the Mac and in Chrome
milestones.quality_bar: The lakes of Red Dead Redemption 2 at dawn: the far shore, the ridge and each tree whole in the water whatever the camera does, joined to its foot at the waterline, softening and stretching as a breeze rises, and never cut off at the edge of the screen.

items.statement: A reflected ray reads the scenery point the true ray meets. For a bank, a post and a hill behind flat water, ripples and 0.3 m waves, seen from 2 m and 10 m, the mirror lookup with two corrections is off by a median of under 0.5% of the ray's length and takes sky for scenery, or scenery for sky, on under 3% of rays, where the design measured 0.09% and 1.3%. On flat water it is exact to a texel of the mirror.
items.ask: Are the true hits traced on the CPU from each surface point's own height and normal, and does the test fail for a lookup with no correction, whose median the design measured at over 10%?

items.statement: A mirrored reflection carries the right light. A matte panel of known radiance standing above the frame, 20 m and 3 km from flat water, reflects with the stored colour the optics equation gives, the air between the panel and the water included, at exposure scales sixteen times apart.
items.ask: Is the expected colour worked out on the CPU with the air of the whole reflected path, and would applying the camera's air to the mirror image a second time fail it at 3 km?

items.statement: On the calm lake at dawn and at noon, with the camera looking down so that the far shore, the ridge and the tree are above the frame, and panning so that they leave its side, their reflections stay whole and do not change. Each joins its foot at the waterline, and nothing fades, stretches or ends at the screen's edge.
